Check or coerce pain drawing data types

Source: R/pdr_match.R
pdr_match.Rd

pdr_match() matches an input against the three pain drawing data types used throughout paindrawr, and either reports which type it is (or whether it is a given type), or coerces it to another type.

Usage

pdr_match(input, action = "eval", as = "", mode = "superficial")

Arguments

input

A variable to be matched against the pdr_tibble, pdr_list and pdr_drawing types.

action

"eval" (default) to evaluate the type of input, or "coerce" to convert input to the type given in as.

as

One of "" (default), "pdr_list", "pdr_tibble" or "pdr_drawing". For action = "eval", the type to test for ("" returns the type as a string). For action = "coerce", the type to coerce to.

mode

"superficial" (default) for a quick structural check, or "validate" for a detailed check of structure and content.

Value

For action = "eval": a string (the type of input, or "invalid") if as = "", otherwise TRUE/FALSE. For action = "coerce": input as a pdr_tibble, pdr_list or pdr_drawing, as requested in as.

Terminology

This is where the paindrawr data types are defined; all other functions refer here.

TermMeaning
pdr_drawingA named list for one drawing, with elements .id, .file, .version, .width, .height, .units, .timestamp, .app, .strokes, .points, and optionally .rgba, .stencil and .stencil_inverted
pdr_listA list of pdr_drawings (typically the list-column pdr_data)
pdr_tibbleA tibble with columns id and a pdr_list column (default name pdr_data)

Required elements of a pdr_drawing:

  • .id (character): unique identifier

  • .width, .height (integer): canvas dimensions

  • .points (tibble): coordinates (required columns .x, .y, .index, all integer)

  • .strokes (tibble): stroke values (required column .index, integer)

Optional: .rgba (numeric array with dimensions height x width x 4).

Matching

With action = "eval" (default) and as = "", the function returns a string: "pdr_tibble", "pdr_list", "pdr_drawing" or "invalid". With action = "eval" and as set to one of the types, it returns TRUE or FALSE for whether input is that type (an input that is NA or NULL gives FALSE).

With action = "coerce", as must be given and the function returns input as that type. Supported conversions: pdr_list to pdr_tibble, pdr_drawing to pdr_tibble, and pdr_drawing to pdr_list. If input already is of the requested type it is returned unchanged; any other conversion, or an NA/NULL input, is an error.

Modes

With mode = "superficial" (default) a quick check of the structure of input is made (a pdr_tibble has columns id and pdr_data; a pdr_list is a list of lists; a pdr_drawing is a list with the required elements). With mode = "validate", a more detailed check of the element types and of the contents of .points, .strokes and .rgba is made (for a tibble, at least one list column must be a valid pdr_list). Invalid .rgba gives a warning.

Examples

pdr_example_data |> pdr_match() # "pdr_tibble"
#> [1] "pdr_tibble"

pdr_example_data |> pdr_match(as = "pdr_tibble") # TRUE
#> [1] TRUE

pdr_example_data |> pdr_match(as = "pdr_list") # FALSE
#> [1] FALSE

pdr_example_data$pdr_data |> pdr_match() # "pdr_list"
#> [1] "pdr_list"

pdr_example_data$pdr_data[[1]] |> pdr_match() # "pdr_drawing"
#> [1] "pdr_drawing"

# Coerce a pdr_list to a pdr_tibble with columns `id` and `pdr_data`
pdr_example_data$pdr_data |>
  pdr_match(action = "coerce", as = "pdr_tibble", mode = "validate")
#> # A tibble: 50 × 2
